package_info.package_name: OKX Binance & Huobi VIP fee comparision.xls / CryptoDashboardV2
package_info.package_manager: malicious Excel macro + MSI installer (Windows ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: The package chain is designed to deliver and execute a multi-stage malware attack: a weaponized Excel file with obfuscated macros drops a secondary payload, which downloads and executes further malware via DLL side-loading and backdoor installation, ultimately enabling remote access, data exfiltration, and C2 communication.

execution_context.trigger: When the user opens the Excel file and enables macros
execution_context.file_location: OKX Binance & Huobi VIP fee comparision.xls (VBA macro)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious macro abuses a VBA UserForm to obfuscate code, extracts a base64-encoded Excel sheet, writes it to C:\ProgramData\Microsoft Media\VSDB688.tmp, and executes it in invisible mode.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the Excel file and enables macros, the macro uses obfuscated VBA code via a UserForm to extract and decode a hidden Excel sheet, writes the decoded payload as VSDB688.tmp to C:\ProgramData\Microsoft Media\, and executes it in invisible mode, resulting in the deployment of a secondary payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The macro leverages obfuscation and hidden UserForms to conceal its actions, writes a hidden file to a system directory, and executes it without user visibility, which are all hallmarks of malicious macro activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Excel macros do not write or execute hidden files in system directories, nor do they use obfuscation or UserForms to hide their logic.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise macros automate file exports, but they do not use obfuscation, hidden directories, or invisible execution.
key_indicators: Executes hidden payloads in invisible mode

execution_context.trigger: Execution of the dropped VSDB688.tmp file

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: VSDB688.tmp downloads a PNG file from hxxps://od[.]lk/d/d021d412be456a6f78a0052a1f0e3557dcfa14bf25f9d0f1d0d2d7dcdac86c73/Background.png, extracts three executables: logagent.exe (legit), wsock32.dll (malicious), and an XOR-encoded backdoor.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon execution of VSDB688.tmp, the code downloads a PNG file from a remote server, extracts three embedded executables (logagent.exe, wsock32.dll, and an XOR-encoded backdoor) from the image, writes them to disk, and prepares them for subsequent execution, enabling the next stage of the attack.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading files disguised as images and extracting executables is a known malware delivery technique to evade detection and bypass security controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not download executables embedded in image files or extract and execute them from such sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some installers may download dependencies, but not in this obfuscated, multi-stage, or covert manner.
key_indicators: Extracts and writes executables from image file
Uses hidden or system directories for payload storage

execution_context.trigger: Execution of logagent.exe in the same directory as wsock32.dll
execution_context.file_location: Directory containing logagent.exe and wsock32.dll (e.g., C:\ProgramData\SoftwareCache\)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: logagent.exe is used to sideload the malicious wsock32.dll, which acts as a DLL proxy to the legitimate wsock32.dll. The malicious DLL loads and decrypts the XOR-encoded backdoor.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When logagent.exe is executed in the presence of wsock32.dll, DLL side-loading occurs, causing the malicious wsock32.dll to be loaded instead of the legitimate one; the DLL then decrypts the XOR-encoded backdoor and loads it into memory, enabling the attacker to establish persistence and execute further malicious actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLL side-loading is a common technique for evading security controls and achieving persistence, especially when a malicious DLL proxies legitimate functionality while loading hidden payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate DLLs should not decrypt or load hidden backdoors, nor should they be used to proxy and execute unauthorized code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: DLL proxying is used in some legitimate software for compatibility, but not for loading or decrypting hidden payloads.
key_indicators: Malicious DLL acts as proxy but loads backdoor

execution_context.trigger: Backdoor loaded by wsock32.dll into memory
execution_context.file_location: Memory (loaded by DLL), possibly written to disk

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: XOR-encoded backdoor, once decrypted, establishes C2 communication with strainservice.com or 198.54.115.248, encodes data, and enables remote access and exfiltration.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After the backdoor is loaded into memory by wsock32.dll, it establishes outbound C2 communication with strainservice.com or 198.54.115.248 over HTTP/HTTPS, encodes and transmits data, and provides the attacker with remote access and data exfiltration capabilities.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure, data encoding, and remote access functionality are classic indicators of backdoor malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not establish covert C2 channels, encode and exfiltrate data, or provide hidden remote access.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may provide access, but are not hidden, encoded, or connected to known malicious infrastructure.
key_indicators: C2 communication to known malicious domain/IP
Remote access and data exfiltration functionality

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: MSI package installs a fake CryptoDashboardV2 app, drops Duser.dll (malicious), which is then side-loaded by a legitimate executable (TPLink.exe), loading an implant.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user executes the MSI installer, it installs a fake CryptoDashboardV2 application, drops a malicious Duser.dll into the installation directory, and arranges for TPLink.exe (a legitimate executable) to side-load the DLL, which then loads an implant for persistence and further malicious activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fake installers that drop malicious DLLs for side-loading by legitimate executables are a hallmark of supply chain and targeted attacks, enabling stealthy persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers do not drop DLLs designed for side-loading by unrelated executables or arrange for implants to be loaded covertly.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some software uses DLLs for plugins, but not in a deceptive or hidden manner, nor for implanting malware.
key_indicators: DLL acts as proxy but loads implant
Installer masquerades as legitimate crypto app

attack_chain.action: User receives and opens weaponized Excel file, enabling macros.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious macro execution and payload drop

attack_chain.action: Macro extracts and executes hidden payload (VSDB688.tmp), which downloads further malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware components downloaded and written to disk

attack_chain.action: Downloaded logagent.exe is executed, side-loading malicious wsock32.dll, which decrypts and loads the backdoor.
Backdoor establishes C2 communication, enabling remote access and data exfiltration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains control and can exfiltrate data

attack_chain.action: User may also execute a fake MSI installer (CryptoDashboardV2), which drops and side-loads another malicious DLL (Duser.dll) for persistence.

behavioral_signatures: Office applications (Excel, Word) creating or executing files in uncommon or hidden directories (e.g., C:\ProgramData\Microsoft Media\)
Office applications downloading files with uncommon extensions or from suspicious domains
DLL side-loading by legitimate executables (logagent.exe, TPLink.exe) with malicious DLLs (wsock32.dll, Duser.dll)
Executables or DLLs making outbound connections to known C2 domains/IPs
Obfuscated VBA macros using UserForms and hidden payloads
Extraction of executables from image files (e.g., PNG) downloaded from the internet
Creation of XOR-encoded or obfuscated binaries on disk
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office applications creating or executing files in uncommon or hidden directories, especially those matching known IOCs. Detect DLL side-loading by monitoring legitimate executables (logagent.exe, TPLink.exe) loading DLLs from user-writable or non-standard locations. Alert on outbound connections to known C2 domains/IPs or on encoded/obfuscated network traffic from suspicious processes. Use EDR to flag obfuscated VBA macros, especially those using UserForms or writing hidden files. Correlate file creation, process execution, and network activity for multi-stage attacks. Additionally, flag extraction of executables from image files and the presence of XOR-encoded binaries on disk.
